transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Mbeki, thank you for coming back into the room to speak with me. I need to discuss something that happened with your son's medication earlier today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mistake made in how we calculated the dose of the medication he received. Instead of weighing him on the scale to get an exact measurement, his weight was estimated. Because of that, he was given a dose that was significantly higher than the safe limit for a child of his size.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. I was the one responsible for the dose, and I failed to ensure the weight was measured correctly. This was my error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is he okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He is stable right now, but we are monitoring him closely because of the high dose.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How long is he staying in?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're concerned about the timing. I can't give you a discharge date this second, but we are watching his vitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have a business to run. I can't be here for a week.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Regarding the medical side, it's important that we track his kidney function and heart rate for the next twelve hours to make sure the drug is clearing his system as expected. Now, just to make sure I explained that clearly, do you understand why the dose was too high?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You guessed his weight instead of weighing him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And that means he got too much medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is the exact plan for the next twenty-four hours. First, we have already started an IV drip to help flush the medication out of his system. Second, the nursing staff will be taking his blood pressure and heart rate every two hours. I will personally review his latest blood results at 6:00 PM tonight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: If the results are clear at 6:00 PM, I will consult with the attending physician to see if we can move him to a lower level of observation. I will come back to this room at 7:00 PM tonight to give you a definitive update on whether he can go home tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need to know for sure tomorrow. I have deliveries to manage.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will give you a clear answer by 7:00 PM tonight. In the meantime, your role is to let us know immediately if you notice him becoming overly sleepy or if his breathing seems different. I've given the nurse a checklist to follow every two hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I also want you to know that I have already filed a formal incident report with the hospital's safety board. We are changing the protocol for this ward so that the electronic health record will block any medication order unless a weight measurement from the last twenty-four hours is entered into the system. This ensures that an estimation can never happen again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That sounds like a good idea.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is an added stress you didn't expect today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's a lot of time away from the shop.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be back at 7:00 PM. Do you have any other questions about the medication or the monitoring plan before I go?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see you then.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, remains regulated during pushback regarding the business, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The error is explicitly named in the second turn, lay language is used, comprehension is checked twice, and no false reassurance is given.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry') and takes full personal responsibility ('This was my error') without deflection.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but does not name specific emotions back to the patient.

T.justification: The resident provides specific steps with timelines (6 PM, 7 PM), defines the patient's role (monitoring sleepiness/breathing), and addresses prevention (EHR blocking).
